reasoning: Leg 4 split is visible in the media wing, not just in state offices. Pattern: institutional media figures face a forced choice between fence-riding (regime-adjacent corporate owners, FCC leverage) and open break. Observed markers: broadcast vanguard purged/neutralized (Kimmel suspension after FCC pressure; Colbert's cancellation following politically-timed criticism, Paramount/Skydance merger pressure), independent media surging as the defection lane (Substack/podcast economics reward visible defiance), Comedy Central/animation wing (South Park) openly mocking the regime while drawing record engagement — the satire wing chose sides. Public trust in mainstream media at historic lows means fence-sitting buys vanguards nothing: audiences punish both conformity and cowardice. The resignations and cancellations are the same mechanism as state pre-positioning: the choice is being forced at every institutional layer, and the fence is collapsing under each of them.
forward_signal: Watch for further resignations from legacy outlets with named successors drawn from the independent lane; watch for FCC/license lever being applied to remaining broadcast vanguards; watch whether social-media platform policy hardens into overt enforcement (the enclosure mutating to control the defection lane itself). If satire and independent media absorb the defection wave while broadcast vanguard hollows, media-Leg-4 split is confirmed as leading the state-level split in timing.
